chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad, he raised it (to the Imam), saying:

It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Why does a person turn/lean to the left in prayer?' He said: 'Because the Ka'bah has six boundaries, four of them are on your left and two of them are on your right; therefore, for that reason, the turning/leaning occurs to the left.'

key_terms.التَّحْرِيفُ: Turning, leaning, or deviation; here referring to the physical movement or orientation towards the left.
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: Salat, the ritual prayer performed by Muslims.
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the cube-shaped structure in Mecca towards which Muslims face during prayer.
key_terms.حُدُودٍ: Boundaries, sides, or corners (of the Ka'bah).

ai.seo_question: Why do Muslims lean or turn to the left during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a geometric explanation for the natural inclination to turn left during prayer, attributing it to the Ka'bah's orientation where four of its boundaries lie to the left of the worshipper. This perspective highlights the interplay between physical orientation and spiritual focus in Shia jurisprudence, suggesting that the leftward bias is not merely a ritualistic habit but rooted in the spatial relationship between the believer and the House of God. Such insights reflect the scholarly tradition of seeking rational and physical causes (*'ilal*) behind religious practices to deepen understanding of their significance.
